steps.t: Call their name and tap both shoulders hard. Watch the chest for up to 10 seconds.
Shout for help. One person fetches the defibrillator and the medical kit.

v.g0: Move them to the restraint board and strap chest and legs. Without a rigid surface behind the back, compressions do nothing.
v.gp: Lay them on their back on the habitat floor.
v.g1: Lay them on their back on a firm surface.

steps.t: Push the centre of the chest 100 to 120 times a minute, 5 to 6 cm deep. Follow the pulsing circle.

v.g0: You have no weight. Hook your feet under the floor loops, or do the handstand method: feet on the ceiling, arms straight on the chest. Alone with no board: Evetts-Russomano method, your legs wrapped around their torso.
v.gp: With little weight your body will not help. Bend and straighten your arms hard.
v.g1: Arms straight, shoulders over your hands. Use your body weight.

steps.t: After every 30 compressions give 2 breaths with the mask, if someone is trained. If not, compressions only.
Defibrillator is here: switch it on, stick the pads on the bare chest and follow its voice. Nobody touches the patient during a shock.

v.g0: Check that nobody is floating against the patient or the board.

steps.t: Swap the person doing compressions every 2 minutes. Do not stop.
Turn them on their side with the airway clear. Check pulse, pressure and oxygen every 5 minutes.

v.g0: Keep them strapped, on their side. Vomit does not drain in 0 g: keep suction ready.

after: Continuous heart monitoring for 24 h
Someone at their side at all times
Send the defibrillator trace to Earth

steps.t: The timer is already running. Do not hold them down. Put nothing in their mouth.
Move them away from edges, panels and loose objects. Cushion the head.

v.g0: Tether them loosely at the waist so they do not drift into equipment. Leave slack for the body to move.
v.gp: Lay them on the floor and clear benches and tools.
v.g1: Lay them on the floor and clear the furniture.

steps.t: Loosen the collar. Notice how it started: one side or both? The doctor will ask.
Look at the timer. Most seizures stop on their own within 1 to 3 minutes.
Past 5 minutes, or a second seizure: the medical officer gives the rescue medication from the kit, at the protocol dose. Get oxygen ready.
Turn them on their side and check breathing. They will wake confused and tired. Speak softly and stay close.

v.g0: On their side and strapped to the board. Suction and bags within reach: in 0 g vomit stays in the mouth.

steps.t: Measure glucose, oxygen, pulse and temperature. Look for a head bump or a bitten tongue.

after: Glucose and vital signs every 30 min for 2 h
No critical task or spacewalk for 72 h
Someone nearby for the next 24 h of sleep
Blood count and a review of current medication

steps.t: Ask: "Are you choking?"
Tell them to cough hard and stay beside them. Do not slap the back while the cough is working.
Give 5 firm blows between the shoulder blades, with the person leaning forward.

v.g0: Hook your feet under the floor loops and hold their chest with your other arm. Otherwise you both spin.

steps.t: Give 5 abdominal thrusts: fist above the navel, pull in and up.

v.g0: Hug from behind with your legs around their waist, or with your feet anchored. All the force comes from your arms.

steps.t: Alternate 5 back blows and 5 thrusts. If they pass out, start CPR.
Keep them seated and breathing slowly. Pain or a cough that lingers after thrusts needs an exam.

v.g0: Collect what came out. A floating fragment can be inhaled by someone else.

after: Abdominal exam by the medical officer
Watch for cough and fever for 48 h

steps.t: Stop everything. Put them in the most comfortable position and loosen tight clothing.

v.g0: Tether them lightly so they spend no effort staying in place.

steps.t: Measure pulse, pressure and oxygen. Run the ECG if the device is at hand.
steps.q: Is the pain a pressure, spreading to arm or jaw, or with sweating and breathlessness?

steps.t: Treat it as a heart attack until proven otherwise. Chewable aspirin from the kit if there is no allergy, per the medical protocol. Oxygen if saturation is below 94%.
Keep the defibrillator switched on beside them.
steps.q: Did they pass out and stop breathing?

steps.t: Repeat vital signs every 5 minutes and note pain from 0 to 10. Send the ECG to Earth.

after: Full rest until the flight surgeon answers
Repeat ECG at 1 h and 6 h

steps.t: Signs: swollen lips or tongue, wheezing, rash, dizziness. If in doubt, treat.
Press the epinephrine auto-injector into the outer thigh and hold for 10 seconds. Through clothing is fine.
Give oxygen if they are short of breath.

v.g0: You cannot raise the legs in 0 g. Tether them and watch blood pressure closely.
v.gp: Lay them down with legs raised. If breathing is hard, let them sit.
v.g1: Lay them down with legs raised. If breathing is hard, let them sit.

steps.t: Give the second dose in the other thigh. Get oxygen and airway gear ready.
Antihistamine and steroid from the kit, per the medical officer. Watch for at least 6 hours: the reaction can return.

after: Observation for 6 to 12 h
Find and isolate the cause
Restock the epinephrine used

steps.t: Gloves and goggles on. Press gauze straight onto the wound, hard, without lifting to look.

v.g0: In 0 g blood forms a dome on the skin, then breaks into floating drops. Cover with an absorbent pad from the start.

steps.t: Hold the pressure for a full 10 minutes.
Arm or leg that will not stop bleeding: tourniquet 5 to 7 cm above the wound. Write down the time.
Apply a pressure dressing. Check pulse and pressure: a fast pulse and cold skin mean heavy loss.

after: Vital signs every 15 min for 1 h
Blood count in 6 h
Clean drops from air and surfaces

steps.t: Do not rub. Remove contact lenses if any.
Rinse the eye for 15 minutes.

v.g0: Use the eyewash goggles: water circulates inside them and is suctioned away. Loose water does not run off the eye in 0 g.
v.gp: Lunar and Martian dust is fine and sharp. Rinse even if it looks minor.
v.g1: Running water, from the nose outward.

steps.t: Cover the eye without pressing. Test vision in the other eye, then do the Amsler grid.

after: Photo of the eye to Earth
Amsler grid daily for a week

steps.t: Stay with them. Speak slowly, in short sentences. Move to a place with less noise and light.
Breathe together: in while the circle grows, out while it shrinks. Two minutes.
Ask them to name 5 things they see, 4 they can touch, 3 they hear. It brings them back to now.
Asking does not put the idea in anyone’s head. It protects.
steps.q: Ask directly: "Have you thought about hurting yourself?" Was the answer yes?

steps.t: Do not leave them alone. Lock away medication and sharp tools. The medical officer takes over and Earth is told at top priority.
Agree on the next 24 hours: sleep, one light task and a private talk with the mission psychologist.

after: Private conference with behavioural health
Critical tasks reassigned for 48 h
Mood check-in twice a day

steps.t: Everyone to the shelter now. Whoever is outside comes in first.

v.transit: Shelter: the central compartment, surrounded by water tanks and cargo.
v.moon: Shelter: the regolith-covered habitat. In the rover, head back to base.
v.mars: Shelter: the habitat. In the rover, head back or park against a cliff.
v.rocket: Rebuild the cargo around the seats, as trained.
v.earth: The atmosphere protects you on Earth. Use this as a drill.

steps.t: Check the personal dosimeters and write down each reading.
Stop all activity outside. Bring water, food and the medical kit into the shelter.
Log each person’s dose. Blood count in 24 hours and again in 7 days: lymphocytes drop first.

after: Blood count at 24 h and 7 days
Dose added to career record
Review this week’s outside plan
when: A solar particle alert or a radiation storm warning is active for the place you are in.
Whoever is outside comes in first. The alert ends only when the alert says so.
watch: Each person's dosimeter reading, written down at the start and at the end
Whether the alert has ended before anyone goes back outside
Blood count at 24 hours and again at 7 days: lymphocytes fall first

standard.text: The design solar particle event stays below 250 mSv effective dose (V1 4031); every exposure as low as reasonably achievable (V1 4029); career dose below 600 mSv (V1 4030).

steps.q: Do they respond when you call?
Is the body stiff or jerking?
Do they have chest pain or pressure?
Are they panicking, crying or not themselves?

steps.t: Measure pulse, pressure, oxygen and temperature. Call the medical officer and note what changed.

care_note.note: window_days, ops and after_days are read from the text of `after`, rounded up to whole days. Illustrative like the rest of this file: not clinically reviewed, to be replaced by flight-surgeon protocols.

eva.n: EVA: when it is suspended or open
when: Before anyone goes outside: on a surface, on a spacewalk or in a rover.
A radiation storm, or a person who is not cleared, closes EVA. Nobody decides alone.
steps: Check the storm banner and this page: EVA is suspended for everyone while a radiation storm is active.
Each person goes only if the medical team has cleared them. A person off EVA stays off, whatever the weather.
Plan the walk with the space weather forecast and the signal delay in mind: help takes as long as Earth takes to reply.
Check suits, tethers and the return route, then tell the crew when you leave and when you are back.
If a storm is called while you are outside, go in first and follow the radiation storm protocol.
watch: The space weather banner and the dose rate of the place
Your clearance: only the medical team sees why someone is or is not cleared
Aerobic capacity against the minimum for the kind of EVA

standard.text: In-mission VO2max at or above 32.9 mL/kg/min for microgravity EVAs (V1 4001) and 36.5 for surface EVAs (V1 4002).

dose.n: Radiation dose and the career limit
when: Every day away from Earth: the dose adds up whether or not a storm is active.
Use it to read the mission dose the crew shares, and to know what a storm adds.
steps: Read your personal dosimeter at the start and end of each day and write it down.
Compare the mission dose with the career limit: it counts every earlier flight, so each person's own career total is in My space.
Plan outside work for the days with the lowest dose rate, and keep every exposure as low as reasonably achievable.
After a storm, log each person's dose and follow the blood count schedule.
watch: Mission dose against the career limit
The daily dose rate of the place: it changes at each leg
The design solar particle event limit of 250 mSv

standard.text: Career effective dose below 600 mSv, the same for all ages and sexes, counting every earlier flight (V1 4030); design solar particle event below 250 mSv (V1 4031); as low as reasonably achievable (V1 4029).

care.n: After an emergency: the care window
when: A Guided Response was closed with a patient named. A care window opens for that person.
This page describes the rule. Who is inside a window stays with the person and the medical team.
steps: Close the Guided Response and choose the patient. Canary opens the window and adds the follow-up items as goals.
For the days of the window, the patient's status is at least the protocol's limit: fit, no EVA, or off critical tasks.
Their alert thresholds are tighter for the same days, so small changes show earlier.
The medical officer reviews the window in the medical console and can close it early.
watch: The follow-up items of the protocol that was used
Any alert that appears during the window
The day the window ends: status returns to what the person's own data says

when: The first hours and days in 0 g after launch: pulse is high, little water drunk, nausea.
Most astronauts go through it. It usually passes in 2 to 3 days.
steps: Take a small sip of water every 15 minutes.
Move your head slowly and fix your eyes on one point.
Keep goals short and patient: rest is part of the plan.
Tell the medical officer if you vomit more than twice.
watch: Pulse and water intake against your own normal
How many times you vomit
Whether it has passed after 3 days

when: The first weeks after months in 0 g, on arriving at a planet's surface or at home.
Lower pressure and a faster pulse than your normal when you stand are expected.
steps: Stand up in two steps: sit, wait, then stand.
Drink 500 mL of salted water in the morning.
No solo suited walks this week.
Measure pressure lying down and standing.
watch: Dizziness when you stand
Pulse and pressure against your own normal
Bone and muscle: the exercise goal changes with the gravity of the place

air.n: Closed environment: air, noise, shared surfaces
when: Every day in a sealed habitat, vehicle or rover: the air is recycled and nobody can step outside.
Several people feeling the same thing at once is a reason to check the air.
steps: If more than one person has a headache or feels drowsy or short of breath, tell the crew and check the cabin air readings.
Move to a part of the habitat with fresh supply while the readings are checked.
Clean shared surfaces and keep the filters on schedule.
Report persistent noise: it costs sleep, and sleep is tracked.
watch: Cabin air readings, when the habitat reports them
Sleep and mood: noise and stale air show up there first
Several people with the same symptom

when: Whenever a message to Earth takes more than a minute each way.
The crew handles emergencies on its own: Earth sees reports after the delay.
steps: Use Guided Response first, then send the report: Earth reads it after the signal delay.
Record messages instead of waiting for a live answer, for work and for home.
Know where the kit is and who is trained, before you need it.
Send what Earth needs to decide in one message: what happened, what you did, what you need.
watch: The reply time shown at the top of the screen
The days since each person last spoke with home
How far the nearest hospital is

operational.note: Operational protocols are reference pages built from what Canary already does: the alerts, the care window rule and the NASA-STD-3001 limits it checks. Illustrative and not clinically reviewed, like the emergency protocols.
